The slide features a large, bold serif title 'Reloc3r' positioned at the top-left. The main body is organized into a two-column structure separated by a vertical dashed line. The left column is dedicated to 'Relative camera pose regression' and contains a detailed architectural flowchart. This flowchart illustrates a dual-stream process where two input images (Image I1 and Image I2) are processed through 'Patchify', 'ViT encoder', 'ViT decoder', and 'Head' blocks to produce relative camera poses. Red dashed arrows highlight 'Weights sharing' and 'Cross-attention' between the two streams. Below the flowchart, there is a 'Key insights:' section with two bullet points. The right column, titled 'Motion averaging', displays a 3D geometric diagram showing various camera frustums and their spatial relationships, accompanied by the subtitle '(A minimalist approach)'. The slide uses a clean white background with moderate text density, relying heavily on diagrams to explain the proposed method.

The slide features a clean white background with a large serif title 'Reloc3r' at the top-left. The main content is split into two distinct sections by a vertical dashed gray line. Two input images (I1 and I2) pass through 'Patchify', 'ViT encoder', 'ViT decoder', and 'Head' modules. Red dashed lines and arrows indicate weight sharing between the encoders and heads, and cross-attention between the decoders. This diagram illustrates multiple green camera frustums (Pd1, Pd2, PdK) and a single blue query frustum (Pq), with dashed lines representing relative pose estimations. The overall text density is moderate, relying heavily on diagrams to explain the methodology.

layout_structure.title_text: Visual comparison of absolute pose estimation
layout_structure.layout_description: The slide features a large, centered title at the top in a black serif font. Below the title, the main content consists of a horizontal arrangement of four visual elements for qualitative comparison. The first three elements from the left are large 3D visualizations showing complex camera trajectories and poses represented by small frustums and connecting lines. Each of these is labeled directly underneath with its corresponding method: 'Map-free (Regress)', 'ExReNet (SUNCG)', and 'Reloc3r-512 (Ours)'. The fourth element on the far right is a vertical stack of three smaller, more linear trajectory visualizations, each labeled to its right with the same three method names for a secondary comparison. The background is a solid white, and the overall text density is light, focusing entirely on the visual representation of the pose estimation results.
